topic: Heimdall: Verified Self-Healing Knowledge Layer for AI Coding Agents

key_points: Primary source: Show HN (2026-08-22, 4 points) — trust-verified knowledge layer for AI coding agents
Persistent memory across every repo/project; one verified kb_search replaces grep/find/ls orientation loop
Trust verdicts on every hit: STRONG / WEAK / REBUILT / STALE — re-verified against live filesystem at query time
Self-healing: moved files re-anchored automatically (REBUILT verdict); deletions retract their own nodes
CPU-only, zero token spend: tree-sitter AST parsing + local bge-m3 embeddings, sqlite, hybrid ranked search (lexical + semantic + graph walk)
Single-writer, level-triggered reconciler (v0.2.0) — nothing tells the graph what changed, only that a path might have
Harness integrations: pi, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf; npm i -g @arihantdeva/heimdall
Runs daily on author's machine across ~12,800 live nodes with a 166-test suite; v0.2.1 on npm
Universal memory layer for AI agents; 63,893 GitHub stars
Per-app/per-user scope, cloud or self-host, LLM-based extraction (token cost)
No trust verdicts on results, no self-healing for moved files
Letta (MemGPT) — platform for stateful agents with advanced memory; 24,375 stars
Per-agent scope, self-host, LLM-based memory management
No trust verdicts, no self-healing re-anchoring
Engram — persistent memory MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor & AI agents; alternative to Mem0 and Zep
Semantic recall, automatic consolidation, bi-temporal knowledge graph, 80% accuracy on LOCOMO benchmark
Modulus — cross-repository knowledge orchestration for coding agents; run multiple coding agents with shared project memory (Show HN, 15 points)
Site currently returns Vercel DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND — availability concern worth noting

angles: The trust-verdict differentiator: STRONG/WEAK/REBUILT/STALE labels make memory results safe to act on — most memory tools return plausible-but-unverified matches
Self-healing knowledge graph: moved files are re-anchored automatically, dead paths pruned — solves the 'rotten anchors' problem other tools ignore
Zero token spend / CPU-only indexing: tree-sitter + local bge-m3 embeddings mean memory maintenance never costs an LLM call or GPU
Cross-repo scope vs per-project tools: knowledge follows the developer across repos, languages, and months
Single-writer reconciler architecture (v0.2.0) as a design lesson: inferring graph mutations from bash hooks collapsed; level-triggered reconciliation fixed it
Comparison vs mem0, Letta, Claude Memory, cAST/grep — Heimdall is the only one with trust verdicts + self-healing + cross-repo + CPU-only
Early-stage caveat: 34 stars, v0.2.1, graft backend dependency for ranked search, MCP server mode still on roadmap
